You are zesty_lantern63, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll first map the documented interface and probe the reference’s main command shapes, then implement a broad first pass in `main.py` and share the discovered behavior with the group.

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). Release binaries are signed with [Sigstore](https://sigstore.dev) via GitHub's artifact attestations. Verify a downloaded binary with the GitHub CLI: ``` gh attestation verify ouch-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo ouch-org/ouch ``` ### Reproducing a release build Release builds are reproducible. Given the source at a tagged commit, anyone can rebuild the same binary and check that it matches what we shipped. Steps: ``` git clone https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch cd ouch git checkout export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --pretty=%ct) export RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$(pwd)=." cargo build --locked --release --target ``` The toolchain version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustup will install it automatically. Cross-compiled targets (anything using `cross-rs/cross`) inherit the cross Docker image's toolchain, which is not pinned by digest yet, so those targets are bit-for-bit reproducible only against the same `cross` image release. ## Compiling from source code Check the [wiki guide on compiling](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Compiling-and-installing-from-source-code). # Benchmarks Benchmark results are available [here](benchmarks/results.md). Performance of compressing and decompressing [Rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) source code is measured and compared with [Hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine). The values presented are the average (wall clock) elapsed time. Note: `ouch` focuses heavily on usage ergonomics and nice error messages, but we plan on doing some optimization in the future. Versions used: - `ouch` _0.4.0_ - [`tar`] _1.34_ - [`unzip`][infozip] _6.00_ - [`zip`][infozip] _3.0_ # Contributing Contributions of all sizes are welcome and appreciated! - Open an [issue](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/issues). - Package it for your favorite distribution or package manager. - Share it with a friend! - Open a pull request. If you're creating a Pull Request, check [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). [`tar`]: https://www.gnu.org/software/tar/ [infozip]: http://www.info-zip.org/ List contents of an archive Usage: ouch list [OPTIONS] ... Arguments: ... Archives whose contents should be listed Options: -t, --tree Show archive contents as a tree -y, --yes Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes -n, --no Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no -A, --accessible Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=] -H, --hidden Ignore hidden files -q, --quiet Silence output -g, --gitignore Ignore files matched by git's ignore files -f, --format Specify the format of the archive -p, --password Decompress or list with password -c, --threads Concurrent working threads -h, --help Print help Compress one or more files into one output file Usage: ouch compress [OPTIONS] ... #!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, sys, pathlib, shutil, gzip, bz2, lzma
from listing import list_archive
from compression import compress
from decompression import decompress_file, formats_for

VERSION = 'ouch 0.8.0'
EXTS = 'tar, zip, bz, bz2, bz3, gz, lz4, xz, lzma, lz, sz, zst, rar, 7z'
ALIASES = 'tgz, tbz, tlz4, txz, tlzma, tsz, tzst, tlz, cbt, cbz, epub, cb7, cbr'
ROOT_HELP = '''A command-line utility for easily compressing and decompressing files and directories.

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  compress    Compress one or more files into one output file [aliases: c]
  decompress  Decompresses one or more files, optionally into another folder [aliases: d]
  list        List contents of an archive [aliases: l, ls]
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help (see more with '--help')
  -V, --version              Print version
'''
COMMAND_HELP = {
'compress': '''Compress one or more files into one output file

Usage: executable compress [OPTIONS] <FILES>... <OUTPUT>

Arguments:
  <FILES>...  Files to be compressed
  <OUTPUT>    The resulting file. Its extensions can be used to specify the compression formats

Options:
  -l, --level <LEVEL>        Compression level, applied to all formats
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
      --fast                 Fastest compression level possible, conflicts with --level and --slow
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
      --slow                 Slowest (and best) compression level possible, conflicts with --level and --fast
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -S, --follow-symlinks      Read from target files instead of from symlinks (relevant for `tar` and `zip`)
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help
''',
'decompress': '''Decompresses one or more files, optionally into another folder

Usage: executable decompress [OPTIONS] <FILES>...

Arguments:
  <FILES>...  Files to be decompressed, or "-" for stdin

Options:
  -d, --dir <OUTPUT_DIR>     Decompress inside OUTPUT_DIR instead of the basename-derived subdirectory
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
      --here                 Extract directly into the current directory, like `tar -xf` and `unzip` do
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
  -r, --remove               Remove the source file after successful decompression
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help
''',
'list': '''List contents of an archive

Usage: executable list [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVES>...

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVES>...  Archives whose contents should be listed

Options:
  -t, --tree                 Show archive contents as a tree
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help
'''}

def die(msg, code=1):
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr); raise SystemExit(code)

def parse(argv, command):
    opts={'yes':False,'no':False,'quiet':False,'format':None,'tree':False,'here':False,'dir':None,'remove':False,'level':None,'fast':False,'slow':False,'follow':False}
    pos=[]; i=0
    takes={'-f':'format','--format':'format','-p':'password','--password':'password','-c':'threads','--threads':'threads','-l':'level','--level':'level','-d':'dir','--dir':'dir'}
    flags={'-y':'yes','--yes':'yes','-n':'no','--no':'no','-q':'quiet','--quiet':'quiet','-t':'tree','--tree':'tree','--here':'here','-r':'remove','--remove':'remove','--fast':'fast','--slow':'slow','-S':'follow','--follow-symlinks':'follow'}
    while i<len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a in ('-h','--help'): print(COMMAND_HELP[command],end=''); raise SystemExit(0)
        if a in ('-A','--accessible','-H','--hidden','-g','--gitignore'): i+=1; continue
        if a in flags: opts[flags[a]]=True
        elif a.startswith('--') and '=' in a and a.split('=',1)[0] in takes:
            k,v=a.split('=',1); opts[takes[k]]=v
        elif a in takes:
            i+=1
            if i>=len(argv): die(f"error: a value is required for '{a}'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
            opts[takes[a]]=argv[i]
        elif a.startswith('-') and a!='-': die(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
        else: pos.append(a)
        i+=1
    if opts['fast'] and opts['slow']: die("error: the argument '--fast' cannot be used with '--slow'\n\nUsage: executable compress --fast <FILES>... <OUTPUT>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['fast'] and opts['level'] is not None or opts['slow'] and opts['level'] is not None: die("error: the argument '--level <LEVEL>' cannot be used with '--fast'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['here'] and opts['dir']: die("error: the argument '--here' cannot be used with '--dir <OUTPUT_DIR>'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['level'] is not None:
        try: opts['level']=int(opts['level'])
        except: die(f"error: invalid value '{opts['level']}' for '--level <LEVEL>': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    return opts,pos

def missing(path):
    die(f"[ERROR] failed to canonicalize path `{path}`: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n - File not found")

def ext_formats(path, override=None):
    if override: return [x.lower() for x in override.split('.') if x]
    parts=pathlib.Path(path).name.split('.')
    return [x.lower() for x in parts[1:] if x]

def main(argv):
    if not argv or argv[0] in ('-h','--help'): print(ROOT_HELP,end=''); return 0
    if argv[0] in ('-V','--version'): print(VERSION); return 0
    if argv[0]=='help':
        cmd=argv[1] if len(argv)>1 else None
        if cmd in ('c',): cmd='compress'
        if cmd in ('d',): cmd='decompress'
        if cmd in ('l','ls'): cmd='list'
        print(COMMAND_HELP.get(cmd,ROOT_HELP),end=''); return 0
    cmd=argv.pop(0); cmd={'c':'compress','d':'decompress','l':'list','ls':'list'}.get(cmd,cmd)
    if cmd not in COMMAND_HELP: die(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{cmd}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    opts,pos=parse(argv,cmd)
    required={'compress':2,'decompress':1,'list':1}[cmd]
    if len(pos)<required:
        args={'compress':'  <FILES>...\n  <OUTPUT>','decompress':'  <FILES>...','list':'  <ARCHIVES>...'}[cmd]
        if cmd=='compress' and len(pos)==1: args='  <FILES>...'
        die(f"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n{args}\n\nUsage: executable {cmd} {'<FILES>... <OUTPUT>' if cmd=='compress' else '<FILES>...' if cmd=='decompress' else '<ARCHIVES>...'}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if cmd=='compress':
        inputs=pos[:-1]; output=pos[-1]
        for p in inputs:
            if not os.path.exists(p): missing(p)
        fmts=ext_formats(output,opts['format'])
        if not fmts:
            die(f'[ERROR] Cannot compress to "{output}"\n - You must supply the compression format\n\nhint: Try adding supported extensions (see --help):\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.tar.gz\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.zip\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can overwrite this option by using the \'--format\' flag:\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output} --format tar.gz')
        try: compress(inputs,output,fmts,opts['level'],opts['follow'])
        except Exception as e: die(f'[ERROR] {e}')
        if not opts['quiet']:
            print(f'[INFO] Compressing "{inputs[0]}"')
            try: print(f'[INFO] Output file size: {os.path.getsize(output):.2f}   B')
            except: pass
            print(f'[INFO] Successfully compressed to "{output}"')
        return 0
    if cmd=='list':
        for path in pos:
            if not os.path.exists(path): missing(path)
            try:
                lines=list_archive(path,opts['tree'])
                if opts['quiet']: lines=lines[1:]
                for line in lines: print(line)
            except Exception:
                die(f'[ERROR] Cannot list archive contents\n - Only archives can have their contents listed\n - Files are not archives: "{path}"')
        return 0
    for path in pos:
        if path!='-' and not os.path.exists(path): missing(path)
        fmts=ext_formats(path,opts['format'])
        if not fmts:
            die(f'[ERROR] Cannot decompress files\n - Files with missing extensions: "{path}"\n - Decompression formats are detected automatically from file extension and signature\n\nhint: Supported extensions are: {EXTS}\nhint: Supported aliases are: {ALIASES}\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can pass an extension to the \'--format\' flag:\nhint:   ouch decompress {path} --format tar.gz')
        try:
            dest,count=decompress_file(path,opts['dir'],opts['here'],opts['format'])
            if opts['remove'] and path!='-': os.remove(path)
            if not opts['quiet']:
                if path=='-': print('[INFO] STDIN decompressed to "ouch-output"')
                else: print(f'[INFO] Decompressed "{path}" to "{dest}"')
                print(f'[INFO] Decompressed {count} files')
        except Exception as e: die(f'[ERROR] Cannot decompress files\n - {e}')
    return 0

if __name__=='__main__':
    try: raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
    except BrokenPipeError: raise SystemExit(1)
